And the record is the standard by which the dead are judged, which raises the question a Christian reader must have answered rather than hurried past. The New Testament holds both sides without flinching: nobody is justified by works of the law (Galatians 2:16), and each will be repaid according to what he has done (Romans 2:6; 2 Corinthians 5:10). They are not in tension once it is clear what each is answering. The books of deeds establish the case, and the case is unanswerable; every person standing there is guilty on the record. The book of life answers a different question: not what did you do, but whose are you.

Where Christians differ: if judgement is by works, how is salvation by grace? Some take judgement according to works as meaning that final salvation depends on our works. Others think that believers are not judged at all. Verdict: everyone is judged according to works, because works reveal what is in the heart. For unbelievers, their works condemn them, because all have sinned (Romans 3:23). For believers, their names are in the book of life; they are saved by grace through faith alone, because Christ has borne their condemnation (Romans 8:1; John 5:24), and their works are the evidence of their faith and the basis of their rewards (1 Corinthians 3:12–15). No one is saved by works; but no one is saved without the works that true faith produces (James 2:14–26). The book of life is what finally decides (v. 15).

Do believers stand before this throne? All the dead stand there, great and small. For believers, the book of life decides: their names are written, and they are acquitted in Christ, while their works are reviewed for reward (2 Corinthians 5:10). Premillennial Christians often distinguish a judgement of believers from this one, separated by a thousand years; the more likely reading is that there is one final judgement, where the book of life separates the saved from the lost, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats in a single scene (Matthew 25:31–46).

What it does not mean. The books of deeds do not mean believers will be shamed by a public display of their forgiven sins. Their sins are removed as far as the east is from the west (Psalm 103:12), blotted out (Isaiah 43:25). They stand clothed in Christ’s righteousness.

Should a Christian be afraid of this day? Serious, yes; terrified, no. A believer should feel the weight of it: every word and deed is known, and how we live matters to the Lord who will review it. But fear of condemnation is not for those in Christ. The Judge on that throne is the Saviour who died for you, and he will not condemn the people he bought. John says that whoever abides in God may have confidence for the day of judgement, because perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:17–18). If you find yourself dreading the throne, do not try to make your file look better. Go to Christ again, today, and rest in what he has done.

Can my name be removed from the book of life? No, if it is truly there. The names were written before the foundation of the world (17:8), by God who does not change his mind, and the Lord Jesus promised the one who conquers, I will never blot his name out of the book of life (3:5). The book is the Lamb’s book because it lists the people he bought with his own blood, and he does not lose what he has paid for (John 6:39). The warnings of Scripture are real, and they are among the means by which God keeps his people trusting; but the believer who heeds them is not one whose name is in pencil.

In a sentence. Then I saw a great white throne and the one seated on it; earth and sky fled from his presence and there was no place for them to go; and I saw the dead, important and unimportant, standing before the throne, and books were opened; then another book was opened, the book of life, and the dead were judged by what was recorded in the books, according to what they had done.

On a Tuesday. You will stand before this throne. Make sure your name is in the Lamb’s book, by trusting him now; and live today knowing that every deed is recorded. Nothing done for Christ in secret is wasted, not the cup of cold water, not the patient answer, not the hidden prayer; it is all in the books, and the Lord who reads them is generous. And nothing done against your neighbour in secret is hidden either. Put right this week whatever you would not want read aloud, and then rest in the fact that for those in Christ, the worst of the file has been answered at the cross.

For worship. Earth and sky cannot stay in the presence of the One on the throne, and yet a sinner washed in the blood of the Lamb can stand there and not be afraid. The books are opened, and every word is in them; and then another book is opened, written before the world was made, and in it are the names of men and women who had nothing to bring but the Lamb’s blood. The Judge of all the earth has already judged their sins, in the body of his Son, on a hill outside Jerusalem. His throne is white with holiness, and his book is written with mercy. Glory to him who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb, whose book it is.

verseByVerse.quote: And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. And if anyone’s name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.

The setting. In the ancient world, people feared being lost at sea, because the body could not be buried, and many thought the dead might be lost for ever. Isaiah 25:8 says God will swallow up death for ever. Paul says the last enemy to be destroyed is death (1 Corinthians 15:26), and that death is swallowed up in victory (1 Corinthians 15:54). Christ holds the keys of Death and Hades (1:18).

And the sea gave up the dead who were in it. Three custodians, and every one of them hands over what it was holding. The sea is named separately for a reason that any first-century reader would have felt at once: to be lost at sea was to have no grave, no body, no name on a stone, the most complete disappearance available. The chapter says the sea gives them up. No one is lost. Even those whose bodies vanished in the sea are raised. All will be judged.

Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them. “Death and Hades”: personified, as in 6:8. Death and the realm of the dead must release everyone they hold. The general resurrection. Nobody is missing. That is the point of listing three, and it reaches every kind of forgotten person: the man whose ship went down, the woman in an unmarked grave, the child in a plague pit, the soldier whose body was never found, the person whose family died out and whose name nobody has said aloud for eight hundred years. Death and Hades kept their records perfectly and hand over the whole file.

And they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. “Each one” (hekastos). John will not let it be a mass. In a scene involving every human being who has ever lived, the judgement is individual: one at a time, on the evidence, by name. Every person answers for himself or herself.

Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. The two figures who rode out at the fourth seal (6:8), the reaper and the one who followed him. The risen Christ said in the first chapter of this book, I have the keys of Death and Hades (1:18), and this is what he does with them. They are not merely disarmed; they are executed. The last enemy is gone. In the new creation, death shall be no more (21:4). Take that as concretely as it deserves. Death is not going to be managed, or explained, or made bearable. It is going to be killed. Everything a reader has lost to it, the funerals attended, the diagnosis that came back, the phone call at four in the morning, was inflicted by something that is itself going to be thrown into a lake and will not be coming back.

This is the second death, the lake of fire. John defines his own term, as he has all through the book (2:11; 20:6; 21:8). The first death separates soul from body; the second is the final, eternal punishment of the whole person, body and soul, separated from all God’s goodness and under his wrath. The promise made to Smyrna, that the one who conquers will not be hurt by the second death (2:11), now has its definition attached, and it is the last thing a reader will want to be uncertain about.

And if anyone’s name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire. “Not found written” (ouch heurethē … gegrammenos). One sentence, and it is the last word of the chapter. Notice that it is stated negatively: not whoever was found, but if anyone’s name was not. And notice the verb: found. Somebody looked. This is the decisive question. Not whether a person’s good deeds outweigh their bad, not sincerity, not how a person compares with his neighbour. A name, in a book, belonging to the Lamb. The book has spent twenty chapters saying that there are two companies and two destinations and that everyone is in one of them, and here the criterion is stated in a single sentence. It should not be blunted.

The question it leaves. This is either the most frightening sentence in Scripture or the most reassuring one, depending on a single question, which every reader is now in a position to ask and which the book will answer directly in two chapters’ time. It is not, have I done enough? Nobody standing at that throne has. It is whether a person has come to the one who says, two chapters later, let the one who desires take the water of life without price (22:17).

Where Christians differ: is anyone saved apart from faith in Christ? Inclusivists hold that some may be saved through Christ’s work without consciously knowing or believing in him, by responding to the light they have; pluralists hold that many religions lead to God. Verdict: the book of life is the Lamb’s book (21:27), and salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). Those who are saved are those who hold the testimony of Jesus and are washed in his blood (7:14; 12:11). This is why the church must take the gospel to every nation, tribe and language (14:6; Romans 10:13–15). God will judge every person justly, according to the light they had (Romans 2:12–16), and no one will be condemned unfairly; but salvation is through Christ alone, received by faith.

What it does not mean. The lake of fire is not annihilation. Those thrown in join the devil, the beast and the false prophet, who are tormented day and night for ever (v. 10). It is terrible, and it should move us to tears, to prayer, and to proclaim Christ.

Is the lake of fire literal fire? The fire is a picture, but what it pictures is worse, not milder. Scripture describes hell as fire and also as outer darkness (Matthew 25:30), which cannot both be literal in the ordinary sense; both are pointing at something real: conscious, unending suffering under God’s just anger, cut off from every good thing he gives, light, love, rest, friendship, hope. A picture is used because the reality is beyond our words. No one should take comfort from the fact that the language is symbolic. The symbols of heaven in the next chapters are not less than gold and pearls; they are more. The same is true here.

What about babies, and people who never heard? Infants who die in infancy are in the hands of a merciful God, and the Reformed confessions teach that elect infants dying in infancy are regenerated and saved by Christ through the Spirit, who works when and where and how he pleases (Westminster 10.3). Many parents have rested on David’s words about his dead child: I shall go to him (2 Samuel 12:23). For adults who never heard, God will judge justly by the light they had, and none will be condemned for not believing a gospel they never heard, but for the sins they knowingly committed (Romans 1:20; 2:12). That does not make them safe; it makes the missionary task urgent. The answer to the question is not speculation but sending.

What about someone I love who died without Christ? This is one of the heaviest griefs a Christian carries, and Scripture does not ask you to pretend. Three things can be said honestly. First, you do not know everything that passed between that soul and God in the last hours; the thief was saved on a cross. Do not pronounce what you cannot see. Second, the Judge of all the earth will do right (Genesis 18:25), and on the last day no one, including you, will think him unjust. Third, your grief is not a lack of faith; Paul had great sorrow and unceasing anguish for his own people (Romans 9:2). Bring it to the Lord, who wept at a grave, and let it drive you to pray for the living.

In a sentence. The sea gave up the dead in it, and Death and the grave gave up the dead in them, and each person was judged according to what they had done; then Death and the grave were thrown into the lake of fire; the lake of fire is the second death; and anyone whose name was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.

On a Tuesday. Everything comes down to one question: is your name in the Lamb’s book of life? If you are trusting Christ, it is. Tell others how theirs can be. Think of one person this week who, as far as you know, is not trusting Christ, and pray for them by name every day; then look for one honest opening to speak of him. And at the next funeral of a believer you attend, remember the end of this chapter: the grave you are standing beside is going to give back what it holds, and the thing that dug it is going into the lake.

For worship. The sea gives up its dead, and Death and Hades hand over every name they ever took, and then they are thrown away like broken tools. The Lord Jesus, who holds their keys because he went into death himself and came out again, empties the grave and kills the killer. And when the books are closed, one book remains open, the Lamb’s book of life: a list of people he bought with his own blood, written before the world was made, and nothing in the other books can get a name off it. Death is swallowed up in victory. Thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

20.text: <sup>1</sup>Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, holding in his hand the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain.<sup>2</sup>And he seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years,<sup>3</sup>and threw him into the pit, and shut it and sealed it over him, so that he might not deceive the nations any longer, until the thousand years were ended. After that he must be released for a little while.<sup>4</sup>Then I saw thrones, and seated on them were those to whom the authority to judge was committed. Also I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received its mark on their foreheads or their hands. They came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.<sup>5</sup>The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were ended. This is the first resurrection.<sup>6</sup>Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection! Over such the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years.<sup>7</sup>And when the thousand years are ended, Satan will be released from his prison<sup>8</sup>and will come out to deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for battle; their number is like the sand of the sea.<sup>9</sup>And they marched up over the broad plain of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city, but fire came down from heaven and consumed them,<sup>10</sup>and the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur where the beast and the false prophet were, and they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.<sup>11</sup>Then I saw a great white throne and him who was seated on it. From his presence earth and sky fled away, and no place was found for them.<sup>12</sup>And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. Then another book was opened, which is the book of life. And the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to what they had done.<sup>13</sup>And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done.<sup>14</sup>Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.<sup>15</sup>And if anyone’s name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.
